sections.title: Positioning
sections.summary: Yotpo sells a retention-marketing suite of reviews, loyalty and, newest, AI visibility: tracking and shaping how AI engines recommend a brand's products.
keyPoints: Homepage: 'Your marketing solutions should work for you. Drive more revenue with best-in-class solutions for loyalty, reviews, and AI visibility.'
The AI angle is the lead: Yotpo Discover tracks how AI engines recommend products, and a dedicated page argues that AI has never tried the product but customers have.
The enterprise page targets ecommerce leaders with authenticated reviews and loyalty programs built for global scale.

sections.title: Products and offerings
sections.summary: Three product lines sold alone or bundled.

rows: Collects and displays reviews with AI summaries, Smart Sorting and retail syndication
Points, VIP tiers and referrals, with Shopify, Magento and other store integrations
Tracks and controls how AI engines recommend products; beta access for enterprise
180+ integrations across email, helpdesk, ads and commerce platforms

gaps: The Visual UGC product and free tools (calculators, generators) were not opened.

sections.title: Pricing
sections.summary: Priced by product and monthly order volume, with a slider on the pricing page. Entry plans are free or low-cost, higher tiers are custom quotes.
keyPoints: Reviews and UGC has a limited free plan up to 50 monthly orders and paid plans from $15 a month.
Loyalty and Referrals has a free plan with paid tiers from $199 a month.
Discover is custom-priced; reviews and loyalty can be bundled to save.
At the default slider position the page shows monthly prices for the two entry reviews plans, with Premium and Enterprise as 'reach out for a custom quote'.

rows: Branded review experience, on-site display, collection and sharing tools
Seller ratings, AI-driven display, AI tools for shoppers, chatbot and email support, product sampling add-on
Reviews AI summary, roles and permissions, translations, syndication across domains, retail syndication
Custom API setup, omni-channel collection, dedicated security and compliance, priority professional services

gaps: Exact plan prices appear only in the live slider widget and were not in the page text.

sections.title: Merchandising
sections.summary: The pricing page works as a configurator: pick a product, set order volume, see the plan. A recommended tag and free entry plans pull visitors in; custom quotes catch the rest.
keyPoints: Tabs for Reviews and UGC, Loyalty and Referrals, AI Visibility and a Bundle sit above a monthly-order-volume slider.
The Pro plan carries a 'recommended' tag; Premium and Enterprise go to sales.
Entry plans are free or low-cost, and bundling reviews with loyalty is offered as a saving.
For merchants: reviews display with AI summaries and Smart Sorting, loyalty points and VIP tiers, referral programs and syndication of reviews to retailers.

sections.title: Technical platform
sections.summary: API documentation and a public API changelog sit alongside 180+ integrations and a help center with a machine-readable index.
keyPoints: API changelog covers App Developer, Core, Loyalty and Referrals, and UGC APIs; the entries surveyed date from March 2024.
The help center publishes an llms.txt index of its documentation.
Integrations page lists Attentive, Omnisend, Gorgias and Klaviyo Customer Hub among featured partners, filterable by product and category.
Loyalty data can be synced through Shopify Metafields.
gaps: The API reference itself was not opened.

sections.title: Design
sections.summary: Bright and approachable: cream backgrounds, big serif headlines on the home page, blue pill buttons and product UI cards. The pricing page switches to a black header and a grey configurator canvas.
keyPoints: Home uses Inter with a blue accent (#0042e4) and pill buttons (100px corners).
Pricing switches to neue-haas-grotesk with a black header and grey canvas.
The home hero pairs a large headline and a business-email field with an AI Visibility card.
Pricing puts a product switcher and order-volume slider above four plan columns.
For merchants: customizable on-site review widgets are listed on higher plans.
gaps: Light and dark modes were not assessed.

sections.title: Company presentation
sections.summary: A trust-and-loyalty-in-the-AI-era story with global reach and named brand outcomes.
keyPoints: About page: 'Leading the next era of trust and loyalty in eCommerce', with 100 countries on 5 continents.
Case studies: Dr. Martens collects 1.8 million reviews; loyalty redeemers spend 15% more, driving a 7.7x return on a loyalty program.
Partner programs for agencies and integration builders are prominent.
gaps: No leadership information in the surveyed pages.

signupPath: No signup button is on the homepage ('Get a demo' beside a business-email field). From the pricing page, 'Sign up' on the Starter reviews plan opens accounts.yotpo.com, a real account form headed 'Create your free account': name, email and password, a 'Continue' button and an agreement to the Terms of Service. The plan is pre-selected in the address. Nothing was entered.

jtbd_fit.evidence: Each product page names its job: collect trusted reviews, grow repeat purchase, win AI recommendations.

capability_visible.evidence: Product pages and a pricing configurator are shown; limited in-product demonstration.

pricing_transparency.evidence: Entry prices and plan contents are published, but exact prices sit in a slider widget and higher tiers are quotes.

product_breadth.evidence: Three product lines with a clear job each and a bundle option.

platform_depth.evidence: API changelog, help center and 180+ integrations; the API reference was not read and sampled changelog entries are from 2024.

time_to_value.evidence: Capture stops before the product; first-value time was not observed.

friction.evidence: Pricing-page Sign up opens a short account form: name, email and password.

trust.evidence: Named brand outcomes and analyst-review mentions.

mobile.evidence: Phone captures exist for home and pricing but were not assessed.

states.evidence: No error or empty states reached.

value_prop_clarity.evidence: The AI visibility framing is new and needs explaining; reviews and loyalty are clear.

proof_quality.evidence: Case-study numbers are specific; 'best-in-class' has no source.

persuasion_integrity.evidence: No urgency tactics; a free tier is stated with its limit.

cta_logic.evidence: 'Get a demo' leads; the self-serve sign-up is found only on the pricing page.

company_narrative.evidence: The trust-and-loyalty-in-the-AI-era story holds from homepage to About to product pages.

offer_packaging.evidence: Four review plans with 'everything in' ladders and a configurator; plan prices sit in a widget.

offer_architecture.evidence: Free entry, recommended middle plan, custom quotes and bundles.

merchant_merch_tools.evidence: Review display with AI summaries and sorting, loyalty tiers and referrals, retail syndication.

visual_craft.evidence: Clear hierarchy and friendly illustration; busy product cards in the home hero.

system_coherence.evidence: Home and pricing use different typefaces and header styles.

merchant_design_control.evidence: Fully customizable on-site widgets on higher plans; branded review experience on Starter.

read.summary: A three-product retention suite repositioning around AI visibility. The pricing configurator and free entry plans are a good model; the weak points are a price list hidden in a widget and an unevenly consistent design.
pros: Free and low-cost entry plans with stated limits.
A product and order-volume configurator on the pricing page.
The signup is a short account form (name, email, password).
cons: Exact prices live inside a widget, not the page text.
AI visibility is a new idea that needs more explanation.
Pricing and home look like different sites.
API changelog entries surveyed date from 2024.
read.howItSells: Sells trust and loyalty as revenue drivers, now framed around being recommended by AI. A free start and a configurator make it feel low-risk.
copy: Offer a free tier with a stated limit.
Use a configurator for volume-based pricing.
Pair product claims with specific case numbers.
avoid: Prices that appear only in an interactive widget.
Two different visual systems for home and pricing.

hypothesis.statement: Showing the entry-plan prices as plain text above the slider will lift pricing-page sign-ups among visitors who do not use the slider.
hypothesis.decisionRule: Ship if sign-ups rise by a pre-agreed margin and sales contacts do not fall over four weeks.

merchandising.summary: A configurator-led ladder with free entry; weaker on showing prices as plain text.
pros: Free entry plan with a stated limit.
Product tabs plus an order-volume slider.
Recommended tag on the middle plan.
cons: Real prices appear only in a widget.

design.summary: Approachable and clear, with a visible shift in style between the home and pricing pages.
pros: Cream backgrounds and big headlines feel friendly and legible.
Blue pill buttons are easy to find.
cons: Pricing swaps typeface and header style.
Home hero crowds an email field and a product card.
